summary: Full backend regression on TaskMint (iter 27). 42/42 tests PASS across auth (device/me/admin login+logout), public content (banners, campaigns, earn-cards, profile-buttons, withdraw-settings, links, maintenance, app-config, version, admob-settings), tasks (checkin, spin+claim, scratch+claim, watch, visit/completed-today), referrals (me + apply happy + error paths), wallet/withdraw (mobile-required, min-amount, wallet-split, daily-cap, refund on reject, approve on successful), campaign submit + duplicate-block + completions listing, and admin (users list, stats, campaign CRUD, completion approve credits user, withdrawal approve/reject, app-config / withdraw-settings / referral-settings / admob-settings PUT round-trips). 1 CRITICAL dead-code bug found in referral withdrawal-mode payout — see rca_of_issue.

critical.issue: Referral withdrawal-mode payout is DEAD CODE. server.py:1927 checks `payload.status == "paid"` and `wd.get("status") != "paid"`, and line 1938 queries withdrawals with `status: "paid"`. But WithdrawUpdate.status Literal is ["pending", "successful", "rejected"] — the model rejects any "paid" input, so this branch never runs. Result: when referral_mode is "withdrawal" or "both", the referrer is NEVER credited on a successful withdrawal. Fix: replace "paid" with "successful" in both places.

minor.issue: Cookie is preferred over Authorization header. This is fine for the mobile app but any browser/session that once received a session_token cookie will keep authenticating as that user until the cookie is cleared, regardless of a different Bearer token supplied. Consider preferring Authorization header when explicitly provided (mobile app is header-based).

action_items: Fix dead-code in server.py:1927 & 1938 — change `"paid"` -> `"successful"` so withdrawal-mode referral bonuses actually pay out.
(Optional) In get_current_user, prefer Authorization header when present, fall back to cookie — avoids the cookie-lingering pitfall we hit while writing tests.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3191 lines — well above the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into modules (auth, tasks, wallet, admin_*, games) before further growth.
SURVEY_QUESTION_BANK and SURVEY_POOL are large inline literals (~150 lines each). Move to a data file.
admin_update_withdraw expects status=="paid" but WithdrawUpdate Literal is ["pending", "successful", "rejected"]. Dead-code bug (see CRITICAL above).
GET /api/earn-cards and /api/profile-buttons return {cards:[...]} / {buttons:[...]} wrappers (confirmed and asserted). Frontend already consumes this shape — no change needed.
seed_data_creation: Created transient TEST_ campaigns per-test-class (cleaned up in class teardown). ~52 anonymous device users generated by _device_login() were pruned post-run via a MongoDB cleanup script. No production/seeded rows were modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter27 regression suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration27_regression.py — reuse it. NOTE: use plain `requests` (no shared Session) for token-based tests because the backend's get_current_user prefers cookie over Authorization header, so a shared Session leaks the last-authenticated user across tests. All admin tests get a dedicated device→admin session in the admin_ctx fixture. To hit the withdrawal-mode referral payout bug, seed a user with `referred_by`, set app_settings.meta.referral_mode='withdrawal' with referral_withdrawal_tiers, submit + admin-approve a withdrawal, then confirm the referrer's balance did NOT change (that's the bug).
rca_of_issue:
BUG: withdrawal-mode referral payout never fires.

Reproduction:
1. Set referral_mode='withdrawal' (or 'both') with a tier {withdrawals:1, points:1000} via PUT /api/admin/app-config.
2. User B applies referrer A's code (POST /api/referrals/apply).
3. B gets 20000 points, sets mobile, and submits a withdrawal.
4. Admin approves it via PUT /api/admin/withdrawals/{id} with status='successful'.
5. Expected: A gains 1000 points. Actual: A's balance is unchanged.

Root cause: server.py:1927 branches on `payload.status == "paid"` and line 1938 filters withdrawals by `status: "paid"`. Neither value can ever be produced by the API — the WithdrawUpdate Pydantic model restricts status to ["pending", "successful", "rejected"]. So the entire referral-on-withdraw block is unreachable. Same for the count in line 1938 (would always return 0 even if invoked).

Mitigation (single-line fix): replace `"paid"` with `"successful"` on lines 1927 and 1938 in server.py. After the fix, add a regression test that seeds referral_mode='withdrawal' and asserts referrer's points_delta > 0 after admin approval.
